text:
maria: FYI seeing GPU tail latency spikes in eu-west-1 around 08:12. Charts show lots of tiny requests (<=8 tokens) causing contention on shared nodes. Anyone else seeing this?

arjun: Which fleet is this on — shared-inference or dedicated?

maria: shared-inference. A handful of tenants with label 'interactive' sending many tiny requests. p95 jumps when runqueue grows.

sophie: Can you paste the node metrics or a short stack/pprof? is the contention memory/compute/PCIe?

maria: quick snapshot below (from 08:10):

```
# node gpu0
gpu_mem_used_pct: 81
gpu_runqueue_len: 24
small_request_qps: 420 -> spiky
host_nic_tx_drops: 4.9%
p95_tail_latency_ms: interactive: 240 -> 520
```

riley: host_nic drops + high runqueue looks like small-request churn + occasional network stalls (NCCL/collectives can amplify). Not pure model compute.

kevin: We should consider two options: carve out a low-latency pool and route interactive tenants there (fewer tenants per GPU), or implement qos-tagging + soft-eviction/weighting in the scheduler. Pool = simpler for isolation but costs more.

arjun: Pool approach is straightforward but expensive. Alternative: add QoS labels and let the router/scheduler prefer packing for batch jobs and spread for interactive. If a big batch hits a node, preempt tiny jobs (soft-preempt) so memory fragmentation doesn't block.

sophie: Another lever is host-level network shaping per-tenant IP range — cap egress so tiny requests don't saturate PCIe/NIC bursts. We can prototype with tc filters.

maria: I prototyped a canary with tc + namespace label-based routing. Patch below — cut p95 by ~30% on the canary hosts in eu-west low-latency pool.

```
# label tenant namespace
kubectl label ns tenant-foo redwood.qos=interactive

# simple tc (host) to cap tenant egress
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 12
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:12 htb rate 200mbit ceil 1gbit
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 u32 match ip src 10.42.7.0/24 flowid 1:12
```

riley: Interesting. Did you see any regressions for batch/throughput jobs co-located on the same host?

maria: Slight increase in per-token latency for large batches when we hit the ceil, but overall application p95 improved for interactive tenants. Need ops sign-off for broader rollout.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: qos-pools + host-tc in eu-west-1 (3 hosts) — monitor dashboards.

kevin: Preliminary cost calc: reserving low-latency pools raises $/gpu ~20%. If we move ~10 customers to the pool, that's roughly +$18k/mo. Recommend opt-in premium tier.

arjun: Action items:
1) prod-test tc across 3 more hosts (riley + maria)
2) router patch: honor X-Redwood-QoS header and prefer low-latency pool (sophie)
3) docs + pricing draft (kevin)
4) runbook for soft-preempt and fallback to shared pool if capacity low (maria)

sophie: I'll own the router patch, aiming for a small canary next week. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll open the runbook and schedule a maintenance window for a gradual canary expansion.

ops-bot: Reminder: please file a short post-canaary incident checklist to the incidents channel once metrics are stable.

kevin: Agreed — tech + pricing decision by EOD next Tue.

maria: Thanks all. Will post a short summary + graphs in #eng-infra once the 24h canary finishes. :eyes:
